items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And they had this apartment, Mike and Shorty Sherlock

ctx.x: Well, now, when I was working with Roy in Chicago, two musicians came from Memphis. One was Tony D'Amico, I believe. He's a pianist, very fine pianist and Mike Bryan, a guitarist. And they used to come to the Three Deuces and see us all the time. When we went to New York they had preceded us, they were already in New York. We went to work on the street, and Mike Bryan was a very fine guitarist. He played in the Van Epps vein. And they had moved -- they had an apartment right up the street from the Kelly's…
And they had this apartment, Mike and Shorty Sherlock

and Sam Rubiwitz, and between sets we would always go up there and we'd smoke a little pot or we'd, you know, and Georgie Auld would be up there every night. And in the meantime Georgie Auld was working with Benny Goodman, and they were looking for a rhythm guitarist, and so I recommended Mike Bryan for the job. Because Georgie used to come down and blow with us every night at Kelly's Stables, you know.
